source.title: Form Array by Concatenating Subarrays of Another Array

teaching.hint: If one group matches in several positions, which choice leaves the most flexibility for later groups?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: For any group, its earliest legal occurrence cannot make a later group harder to place than a later occurrence would.
solution_outline.approach: Advance through the groups in order, searching from the end of the preceding accepted match. Choose the first full match and continue after it; fail if none exists.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The cursor is the first unused position. After each group, it is no farther right than the cursor of any complete valid placement for the same prefix of groups.
solution_outline.correctness: By induction, a valid placement of the next group at a later position implies the earliest match exists at or before it. Advancing past the chosen match preserves disjointness and ordering. Failure therefore rules out every placement.
solution_outline.complexity: O(mL + S) time and O(1) auxiliary space, where m is the length of nums, L the longest group, and S the total group length; bounds are at most about one million comparisons.
solution_outline.pitfall: Allowing a later match to overlap the end of an earlier group violates the disjointness rule.

common_wrong_turns: Choose a later occurrence without considering its effect on remaining space
Resume the next search inside a prior match
source_fidelity_notes: Removed verbose marked-up examples; retained ordered, disjoint matches and small comparison bounds.
